title: Physical and mathematical models
subtitle: Four kinds of model, and how a differential equation becomes a program.

types.title: Kinds of model
types.body: Physical models are scaled or analogue versions of the real thing — static (a scale model of a building) or dynamic (a wind tunnel, a circuit that mimics a mechanical system). Mathematical models describe behaviour with equations — static (an algebraic relation such as Ohm’s law) or dynamic (differential equations in time). Computers make the dynamic mathematical model the workhorse.

ode.title: From a differential equation to a simulation
ode.body: Most dynamic models are of the form dy/dx = f(x, y). Euler’s method advances in small steps: yn+1 = yn + h·f(xn, yn). Runge–Kutta 4 uses four slopes per step and is far more accurate. For y′ = x + y, y(0) = 1 (exact y = 2eˣ − x − 1), at x = 1 with h = 0.1: Euler gives 3.18748, RK4 gives 3.43656, exact 3.43656.
ode.steps: One Euler step from (0, 1) with h = 0.1 for y′ = x + y. Slope f(0,1) = 1, so y₁ = 1 + 0.1·1.

pde.title: Partial differential equations: heat flow
pde.body: When the state varies in space as well as time we have a PDE. The heat equation ut = α uxx is discretised on a grid: uiⁿ⁺¹ = uiⁿ + r(ui−1ⁿ − 2uiⁿ + ui+1ⁿ) with r = αΔt/Δx². The explicit scheme is stable only for r ≤ ½. A rod with ends held at 100 and 0 relaxes to the straight line between them: mid-rod temperature 49.997 after 400 steps (steady value 50).

mech.title: A physical model in the notebook: a damped oscillator
mech.body: SIMBLIP’s physics engine is itself a dynamic physical model solving Newton’s second law. A mass on a spring obeys m x″ + c x′ + k x = 0; the solution oscillates with angular frequency ω = √(k/m) and decays if c > 0. Press Simulate and compare the period with 2π√(m/k).

use.title: Choosing a model’s level of detail
use.body: A model should be as simple as the question allows. Include what affects the answer; ignore the rest, and state the assumptions (no air resistance, small angles, constant service rate). Validate by comparing with data; refine only where validation fails.

summary.title: Summary
summary.body:
• Physical vs mathematical, static vs dynamic.
  • ODEs: Euler is simple, RK4 accurate; PDEs: discretise space and time, watch stability.
